title: How Can Video Generative AI Transform K-12 Education? Examining Teachers’ Perspectives through TPACK and TAM
extended_summary:
This paper examines how K-12 teachers perceive the educational potential, limitations, and implementation needs of video generative AI (Video GenAI). The authors frame the study around two established models, TPACK and TAM, to understand how teachers judge the technology’s pedagogical fit, ease of use, usefulness, and willingness to adopt it in classroom practice.

The study is not an intervention trial; instead, it asks teachers to interact with a video generation system, Luma Dream Machine, and then reflect on their experiences in semi-structured interviews. The sample includes ten participants: elementary school teachers, one high school teacher, and one former elementary teacher/data analyst, all in South Korea. Participants also received an educational guide with example prompts and subject-specific use cases before interviews.

Findings suggest that teachers saw promise for Video GenAI in creating visual explanations, supporting creative expression, diversifying project-based learning and assessment, and helping students develop AI literacy. At the same time, they raised concerns about output quality, hallucinations, language limitations, safety, copyright, age restrictions, infrastructure, and lack of teacher-monitoring features. Overall, the paper is descriptive and theoretical rather than causal; it offers early-stage evidence about teacher perceptions of generative AI video tools, not evidence of learning impacts or comparative effectiveness.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study with purposively selected teachers and no experimental manipulation or causal identification. It is methodologically structured, but evidence is descriptive and perception-based rather than causal.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful educational and institutional implications for K-12 use of video GenAI, but it reports no measured student outcomes or effect sizes. Its impact is therefore plausible but unclear rather than demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: Qualitative teacher-perspectives study of video generative AI (Luma Dream Machine) for K-12 instructional use, including creating subject-specific educational videos, student creative production, and teacher-designed tasks rather than lesson-plan generation or feedback.

finding.finding_summary: Teachers viewed video GenAI as promising for subject learning across science, history, Korean language, and other K-12 areas by helping visualize abstract concepts and create tailored instructional materials. This is a qualitative perception study with no experimental effect size reported (n=10 teachers).
finding.measure: Teacher interviews about perceived educational potential for subject learning and comprehension

finding.finding_summary: Teachers expected video GenAI to increase student engagement, motivation, and willingness to participate in classroom activities, especially through visually rich and novel content. No quantitative effect size was reported; evidence is based on interview themes from n=10 teachers.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported expectations of student engagement and motivation

finding.finding_summary: Participants believed video GenAI could support creativity, divergent thinking, composition, and project-based learning, and could also strengthen AI literacy and prompt formulation. These are qualitative findings from teacher interviews (n=10), with no effect size reported.
finding.measure: Teacher interview themes on creativity, divergent thinking, AI literacy, and project-based learning

finding.finding_summary: Teachers reported that video GenAI could reduce preparation time by generating supplementary instructional materials more quickly and easily than traditional video production. The paper provides qualitative perceptions only (n=10) and reports no quantitative effect size.
finding.measure: Teacher perceptions of preparation time, ease of creating instructional media, and workflow efficiency

finding.finding_summary: Teachers identified both enabling conditions and barriers for adoption, including ethical safeguards, age restrictions, parental consent, copyright, infrastructure, funding, and institutional support. The paper is descriptive/qualitative and reports no effect size; findings are based on interviews with n=10 teachers.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported policy, governance, infrastructure, and institutional readiness concerns
